paragraphs: Fresh, excluded SQLite 3.53.2 profiles confirm the kept plans. The default Session summary falls from 196,961 full-scan / 1,999,467 VM steps to 4,129 / 85,802; its statement time is 233.6→17.0 ms. The served checkpoint falls from 764,212 / 7,639,765 to 4,401 / 267,049, with statement time 891.8→111.6 ms. These are store/sqlite/sessions.rs::session_summaries_in using task_work.rs::session_tasks; both Task indexes appear in HEAD’s bound plans. Served figures use the second summary execution, inside the timed checkpoint, excluding the initial frame.

Wave live-agent inventory falls from 160,529 full-scan / 675,261 VM steps to 60 / 2,205, and 194.7→0.4 ms, through processes.rs::agent_processes and agent_process_unfinished. Task Process membership falls from 175,599 / 7,655,559 to 15,070 / 279,500, and 350.9→9.1 ms, through task_work.rs::lf_process_ids and processes_cwd equality/range probes. Work selection’s summary falls from 764,212 / 7,642,754 to 4,401 / 270,038, and 934.3→115.1 ms. Board’s leading substantive query counters remain unchanged.

The removed default-list statement work is 216.6 ms, close to the paired command’s 208.2 ms median reduction. In the separate profiled baselines, that statement occupies 26.4% of CLI time; the served summary occupies 80.3%, the Wave inventory 40.0%, and Work-selection summary 55.7%. Removing each entire piece caps improvement at those shares in those runs. Profiled served, Wave and Work paths fall 74.7%, 17.1% and 50.9%, within those ceilings. The profiled CLI falls 39.4%, which the summary alone cannot explain: other elapsed costs and instrumentation differ between those two runs. That profiled CLI wall-time difference is inconclusive and is not used as the speed estimate. The uninstrumented five-pair claim is supported by the matching outputs, separated ranges and independently observed 216.6 ms of removed query work; profiler times do not exactly decompose its latency.

Task-status native samples retain the same attribution: Keychain reads fall from 4,025/7,094 (56.7%) main-thread samples to 37/841 (4.4%); check_scope falls from 1,613/7,094 (22.7%) to 4/841 (0.5%). The source paths are waves.rs::task_detail → human_session::listed → LaunchCapacity and linear_observe::check_scope → planning_client::repository_scope. Capacity, scope and SQLite occupy 89.4% of baseline samples counted as a union, without nested double-counting. The sampled commands fall 85.1% (9,869.9→1,473.0 ms), below that approximate ceiling. Stack shares are not a wall-time decomposition. HEAD’s next limiter remains RepoId::discover during planning field delivery: 303/841 samples (36.0%); sqlite3_step accounts for 207/841 (24.6%). These overlapping profile views are not added.

Lock scope in the fresh profiles: neither Session-list path issues BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Each network-denied Task-status profile does so once for linear_team_checks, then rolls back; acquisition takes 0.0026 ms before and 0.0025 ms after. Those Task reads can take the writer lock, but these runs show no long wait and do not reproduce the Session-list stall.
